title: Female borrowers who mention a supportive husband helping with repayment may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who combine a geographical greeting with gratitude may fund faster.
Female borrowers who provide specific details about their lending institution may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who explicitly state they have no dependent children may fund faster.
Mentioning specific details about the number or ages of children predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention specific institutional affiliations or local branches may fund faster.
Details about children may accelerate funding for men but slow it for women.
Female borrowers who mention specific ages of children or education needs may fund faster.
Pitches from women that explicitly state the number of years the business has been operating are associated with increased funding speed.
Female borrowers who include gratitude markers thanking lenders may fund more slowly.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayment predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Providing specific operational or inventory details predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who include loan amounts in local currency fund more slowly.
Specifying the number of years a business or trade has been operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
